page.title: Virtual Events Checklist: What to Include
page.description: A practical checklist covering registration, live engagement, recording, replay delivery and post‑event follow‑up so you can launch virtual events on time and capture leads.
page.h1: What belongs on a virtual events checklist?
page.definition: A virtual events checklist is a structured list of tasks, owners and deadlines that covers registration, live production, recording, replay distribution and post‑event follow‑up so nothing is missed from planning through to lead capture. It also flags early‑warning signals for late assets and schedule risk.
page.quick_answer: Assign one owner to each checklist item, run a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live, and send the replay within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours.

sections.h2: What registration steps belong on a virtual events checklist?

blocks.p: Start with a registration workflow that captures attendee data, confirms attendance and feeds the CRM. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

ul: Create a branded landing page with clear value proposition
Set up automated confirmation email with calendar invite
Integrate registration form with HubSpot or Salesforce

sections.h2: How do you plan engagement and interaction during the live event?

blocks.p: Design interaction points that keep attention high and generate data for follow‑up.

ul: Schedule live polls at each major agenda segment
Open moderated Q&A with a dedicated moderator
Capture real‑time sentiment via emoji reactions

sections.h2: Which recording and replay tasks must be completed after the event?

blocks.p: Lock down recording delivery so the replay reaches attendees while the experience is fresh.

head: Task
Owner
rows: Start cloud recording at session start
Edit recording into full replay and highlight clips
Upload assets to hosting platform and embed on site
Send replay email with personalized links

sections.h2: What follow‑up actions turn attendees into owned audience?

blocks.p: Convert live attention into a permission‑based list that you can nurture.

ol: Add high‑intent contacts to nurture workflow
Deliver on‑demand content hub with gated assets
Schedule sales outreach for qualified leads

sections.h2: What early‑warning signs indicate late assets or schedule risk?

blocks.p: Monitor the production timeline for bottlenecks that could delay go‑live.

ul: Speaker slides not received two weeks before rehearsal
Run of show missing cue times three days out
Backup encoder not tested one day before event
Registration numbers far below target five days prior
Platform access credentials not shared with crew

faq.q: How far in advance should the run of show be finalized?
faq.a: Finalize the run of show at least two weeks before the live date so the producer, speaker manager and platform operator can rehearse cues, test transitions and confirm backup stream readiness.

faq.q: What is the minimum staffing for a simple webinar?
faq.a: One producer can manage a straightforward webinar, handling the run of show, speaker cues, Q&A moderation and backup stream monitoring without additional crew.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Distribute the replay within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours after the event ends, while the content is still top of mind and engagement metrics are highest.

faq.q: Which tools help track checklist completion across teams?
faq.a: Use Asana, Monday.com or Airtable for task ownership, due dates and status visibility; link each item to the run of show document in Google Docs or Notion for quick reference.
